Benton County: 224 people in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025
HUD counted 134 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Benton County in 2025.
Reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Benton County, Minnesota, included 224 people in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 51 from 275 in 2024. Those households numbered 134.
HUD classified 44% of those households as headed by a person from a racial or ethnic minority group. Households paid an average of $438 a month toward rent and utilities, down $6 from $444 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $18,091, down $527 from $18,618 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families receiving Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the . That average covers families who obtained assistance, not applicants still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
